Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1862 Pustet antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: 1962 reads `Beatorum` where 1862 reads `BEat6rum`; 1962 reads `pariterque` where 1862 reads `parit6rque`; 1962 reads `Cornelii` where 1862 reads `X.`; 1962 reads `Cypriani` where 1862 reads `N.`; 1962 reads `Domine,` where 1862 reads `D6mine,`; 1962 has nothing there; 1862 has `:`; 1962 reads `eorum commendet` where 1862 reads `e6rum comm6ndet`; 1962 reads `veneranda.` where 1862 reads `venerdnda.`; 1962 reads `Dominum.` where 1862 reads `D6minum.`; THE TWO SAINTS' NAMES: the 1862 does not print `Cornelii et Cypriani` inside this formula. Its Common leaves the slot as N. et N., and its 22 April Mass fills the same slot with a different pair. Every other word of the 1962's oration stands in the 1862 verbatim, in two places.; against the 1862's 22 April printing: 1962 reads `Beatorum` where 1862 22 April reads `BEat6rum`; against the 1862's 22 April printing: 1962 reads `pariterque` where 1862 22 April reads `paritSnjue`; against the 1862's 22 April printing: 1962 reads `Cornelii` where 1862 22 April reads `Soteris,`; against the 1862's 22 April printing: 1962 reads `Cypriani` where 1862 22 April reads `Caji`; against the 1862's 22 April printing: 1962 reads `quaesumus, Domine,` where 1862 22 April reads `qua?sumus D6mine,`; against the 1862's 22 April printing: 1962 reads `eorum` where 1862 22 April reads `e6rum`; against the 1862's 22 April printing: 1962 reads `Dominum.` where 1862 22 April reads `D6minum.`; 1862 sets a comma after `Martyrum` and none after `quaesumus`; the 1962 reverses both; 1862 conclusion is the short cue, and so is the 1962's here (the Commune prints the longer one at no. 4239/4243). Corroboration: 1862 in two places (Common and 22 April); the 1962's own Commune at printed pp. 737 and 744 prints the same formula with N. et N. The 1922 Mame prints no proper oration for Cornelius and Cyprian either -- its 16 September (printed p. 716, PDF p. 830) sends the Mass to the same Common and prints only the Euphemia commemoration..
